newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity follows natgas futures to end up.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity follows natgas futures to end up.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended higher following a rise in natural gas futures and strong western physical electricity prices, industry sources said.
"It was mostly driven by gas and the cash prices are still strong," said one futures broker.
Electricity futures followed NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures lower in morning trade then later recovered, though not as strongly as the Hub gas prices.

Spot peak power prices in the Southwest for next day delivery were said to have risen Tuesday to $27.00-28.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) while spot prices in the Northwest were reported to have held steady near $29.25-29.75 per MWh.
Spot San Juan physical gas was said to be trading near $3.15 per million British thermal units, rebounding from some reported talk at $2.90.

January Palo Verde (PV) electricity futures settled 44 cents higher at $24.63 per MWh after trade in a range of $23.50-25.10, while February ended up 45 cents at $20.25 from trade in a range of $19.25-20.50 per MWh.
January California Oregon Border (COB) finished up 40 cents at $25.00 after trade in a range of $23.50-25.25, while February ended up 10 cents at $19.60 from trade as low as $19.25 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds closed steady to up to 60 cents higher.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 290 COB and 222 PV contracts traded Tuesday.
